articleTitle: Phishing Attacks and Preventions in Blockchain Based Projects
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: With the development of Internet technologies, the number of threats and attacks directed at networks and systems is increasing. Attackers invent new ways of attack or improve old ones. One of the most common serious threats is "Phishing", in which cybercriminals attempt to steal user credentials using fake emails or websites or both. Blockchain projects increasingly becomes the target of attacks by intruders due to high investments and gaps in national legislation. After a series of attacks on blockchain projects around the world, the issue of cybersecurity of blockchain became particularly relevant. The article classifies the main types and schemes of phishing attacks on the blockchain, suggests methods of protection against them, examines the development of blockchain protection against phishing attacks.

Author Keywords: blockchain, phishing, cryptocurrency, security, malware, social engineering

articleTitle: Fuzzy-PID Controller for Two Wheels Balancing Robot Based on STM32 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: In this paper, a fuzzy-PID controller is proposed to regulate the movement of two wheels balancing robot. The fuzzy-PID controller is a combination of a fuzzy controller and PID controllers for the balancing and movement or distance of the two wheels balancing robot. The fuzzy controller is designed based on relation models for the robot's balancing. The PID controllers are proposed to control the robot's position. The whole fuzzy-PID is ported and run on a real-time operating system using an STM32F4 Discovery Kit. The received results showed advantages of the fuzzy-PID controller.

articleTitle: Directed Fuzzing Based on Program Dynamic Instrumentation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: In this paper we present a new approach for directed fuzzing. It enables faster generation of the input data for the target program's specific instructions execution. Existing fuzzing tools randomly generate or mutate input data to increase code coverage. This approach is not effective for analysis of special code regions. The basic idea behind of this paper is to instrument target program in a such way that interesting code fragments were executed as soon as possible. For that propose we detect all the paths in the program which are connecting program's entry point to the considered instructions. Then we apply two type of instrumentations. In the first case we insert coverage collection instructions only in detected paths, which enables fuzzing tool to consider generated or mutated input data valuable if the distances between executed blocks and target points are reduced. In the second case we additionally insert 'exit(0)' instructions in those basic blocks from which target points are unreachable and their execution has no any influence. It allows repeatedly increase fuzzing speed.

Author Keywords: directed fuzzing, instrumentation, static analysis, path detection

articleTitle: User Tracking in VR Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Recent development in the field of virtual reality technology brought new possibilities and exploitation of the old concept of stereoscopic projection. This 3D representation in combination with motion tracking of users and real-time interaction is present in actual products, such as HTC Vive, Oculus and Playstation VR, that are primarily dedicated for game industry. The research is focused on embracing the new possibilities of this technology, enabling to track the user's interactions in much immersed and interactive environment. This shift from pure observation of the environment to interaction with it allows us to better undrestand the user's space perception and decision making. During the experiment users were observed in the virtually modeled, well-known architectural icon, Barcelona Pavilion by Mies van der Rohe. The installation took place at computational design festival Sensorium in Bratislava and examined the concept of virtuality and reality as two opposites. Users were invited to take photographs in this pavilion, which reflected on recording the most interesting motives. Case studies focused on possibilities of using VR as a tool of analysis and design. Data gathered from user motion tracking and taken photographs were analyzed and evaluated to explore relations between motion and motivation in virtual space and relations in behavioral patterns of users to support the concept of movement in space as crucial aspect of space perception.

articleTitle: HRS-100 Hybrid Computer: History of Creation and Application Experience
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Hybrid computing systems are an attempt to combine all the best inherent in analog and digital technology, and to avoid their shortcomings. The article is devoted to the history of the development and practical application of one of the successful models of a hybrid computer.

Author Keywords: history of computing, analog computer, hybrid computer, simulation, computer science

articleTitle: The Main Problem of Photovoltaic Energy and Possible Ways to Solve It: Historical and Technical Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Despite the numerous developments of new technologies in the field of photovoltaic energy, the share of silicon technology in the world market for many years is more than 90%. If you rely on existing forecasts, this situation will continue in the future. However, there is a contradiction between the projections of energy development and the requirement to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. The predicted value of the share of renewable energy in the world by 2050 is 50%, and to prevent the increase in temperature on Earth by 1.5 degrees required to bring carbon dioxide emissions to zero. Thus, a sharp increase in the production of silicon and solar modules based on it is necessary. The report examines the existing forgotten and undervalued technologies for the production of silicon-based solar modules, reducing the need for this material and increasing the efficiency of the modules.

Author Keywords: photovoltaic, silicon, carbon dioxide emissions, matrix solar cells, rhizogrid modules, HIT technology, scale effect

articleTitle: Development of Innovative Technologies in Russian Agro-Industry
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: This paper analyses the application of scientific and technological innovations to Russian agroindustry. This process was successfully launched by the 'machinery revolution' of the 1920s, the use of protophytotrons and inductive mutagenesis in plant breeding in the 1930s, and the adoption of radionuclides method for agricultural monitoring in the 1940s. The development of this trend was then delayed by the spread of Lysenkoism in the 1940-1960s. However, from the 1980s, a global strategy of 'precision agriculture' (PA) evolved, which was related to the ecological and energy-saving approaches towards agroindustry practice. These approaches relied heavily on space agricultural technologies in the USSR in the 1970-1980s. PA strategy is based on the use of global positioning systems, geographic information systems, as well as sensors for remote measurements and onboard sensors that command agricultural machinery. This paper discusses the contribution of the Soviet scientists and engineers to the development of technological innovations, including PA, as well as obstacles to, and issues with, their application in Russia.

Author Keywords: agro-industry, the USSR, 'machinery revolution', high-yielding varieties, inductive mutagenesis, 'chemicalisation' of agro industry, radionuclides in farming, 'green revolution', space agricultural technologies, 'precision agriculture

articleTitle: The Impact of Nikola Tesla's Patents to Development of Modern Mobile and Internet Services
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Nikola Tesla has been known as a Serbian scientist and inventor who has made a great impact by designing modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply systems. However, it is less known that his patents in the field of communications represent a basis of present-day ICT systems. In this paper, we present Tesla’s most important patents and results regarding mobile and wireless communications and Internet services: patents concerning transmission lines, radio technologies, logic gates and digital modulations. We analyze the patents related to frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS), orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), and wireless cryptography in details. In addition, we present Tesla's vision of communication services that have become possible to implement almost a hundred years later.

Author Keywords: Nikola Tesla, patents, wireless communications, internet services

articleTitle: The Makers of the GOELRO Plan
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The political orientation of the GOELRO Commission members engaged in the development and implementation of the country's electrification program is considered. The social status of I. G. Alexandrov, B. E. Vedeneev, A. V. Vinter, G. O. Graftio, G. M. Krzhizhanovsky and other outstanding power engineers is investigated.. Attention is paid to the industry as a whole, and its most important structural and technological subsystems: design, construction, installation, operation and repair of equipment in the heat, hydro and electricity. The analysis of life and activity of energy elite is executed in the context of the largest events in the history of the country. Materials of archives, branch periodicals, scientific monographs and memoirs are used as a source base.

articleTitle: Automatic Creation Technologies of Declarative Tools for Clustering Media Documents
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article describes the methods of identifying the conceptual content structure of the dataset of documents for the clustering. It was found that in the automatic extraction of key text concepts it is necessary to use the criteria of semantic significance of words and phrases obtained on the basis of syntactic, statistical and semantic methods. The syntactic criteria are based on the definition of the syntactic role of words and phrases in the text dataset. We accent on those elements of sentences that forms its semantic (predicate-actant) structure. In this research four methods of automatic identification of key text concepts have been elaborated, their comparative analysis is carried out and the technology of automatic creation of declarative means for text clustering of media is developed. The precision assessment of document clustering with and without declarative methods is conducted on test dataset.

Author Keywords: document clustering, automated text processing, formal text description, linguistic software, declarative tools, key text concepts

articleTitle: Creating Geo-Information Base of an Internet Resource "Ancient Waterways in the North-West of Russia"
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Nowadays, all kinds of gadgets open up new possibilities for presenting information online. The geoinformation base of the Internet-site "Ancient waterways in the North-West of Russia" allows a wide range of users to get more information about waterways at any time. This Internet resource is unique in Russia.

Author Keywords: Ancient waterways, North West of Russia, geo information base, internet resource

articleTitle: Electrochemical Enterprises and Industrial Technologies in the Context of the Industrialization Policy in the USSR
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The paper analyzes the process of assimilation of new technologies and methods in the main heavy industry sectors in the USSR during the early five-year plans, as exemplified by the case of electrochemical technologies. It is emphasized that the development of power industry, nonferrous metal industry, and mechanical engineering was linked to, and interdependent with, the possibilities for widespread implementation of electrochemical technologies. The development of the fundamentals of electrometallurgy of aluminum by the Leningrad school led by P.P.Fedotiev is reviewed as one of the first examples of industrial use of electrolysis. The factors that prompted the development of electroplating are analyzed. It is shown how industrial development strategies set out in the Five-Year Plans shaped the development of this area as multisectoral production and how this structure created problems for the future.

articleTitle: Russian Electronics: Globalization and National Interests
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: After the collapse of the USSR (1991) the production of electronic products in Russia decreased, and imports of foreign electronics grew up. Since the beginning of the 2000s, attempts were made to determine an optimal way for development of the domestic electronic industry, and concentration of the financial efforts on the key areas of this development. Enterprises of the electronic industry are also currently engaged in the diversification processes - an increase of the share of civilian electronics products in the production.

articleTitle: Impact of Socio-Economic and Psychological Factors on the Development of Fiber Optic Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of non-technical factors affecting the development of fiber-optic communication systems. It discusses the role of socio-economic factors in stimulating a new round of technical development of communication systems in the late 2000s and the emergence of coherent systems. Author analyses the stages of development of coherent systems in the second decade of the XXI century and reveals the influence of psychological factors on the emergence of a new class of coherent systems using two optical carriers. It is shown that the choice of a technical solution using two carriers was caused, first of all, not by the internal logic of technology development, but by the marketing need to accelerate the achievement of a psychologically significant transmission speed of 400 Gbps.

articleTitle: Legal Issues of Creation and use of 3D-Documents in Russian Federation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: With the development of technology, not only photo and video, but also digital 3D-models of objects have become widespread. The development of computer technology is quickly ahead of the legal regulation of relations about innovative IT-applications. There are difficulties in determining intellectual rights for a 3D-model, since the data underlying the creation of such a model may belong to various individuals and entities. It is necessary to adopt an independent definition of a 3D-document and determine its legal regime, including the standards of the requisites of such a document and the regulations for transferring it to archives and other actions with it.

articleTitle: Soviet-French Scientific and Technological Cooperation Aboard the Salyut-7 Space Station
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The scope of this article is to cover two projects in the field of astrophysics and geophysics photography technology designed by French scientists and operated on board the orbital station Salyut-7 by a Soviet-French crew during the first joint cooperation programme, PVH (Premier Vol Habité, 24 June-3 July 1982). A scientific mission aiming at achieving biomedical, metallally experiments and astronomical photography at a low earth orbit, PVH includes the development of prototypes instruments in each domain that would reach the objective of producing science on a global scale. Especially in astronomy and geophysics, observation and photography in the visible and near-infrared, made possible from space, required the innovation of a high sensitivity imaging cameras, called after their experiments PIRAMIG and PCN. Innovating technology consists then, in optimizating a photographic chamber developed previously for ballons observation programmes with higher sensitivity component, enabling the imaging of weak emission of light originated in the stratosphere and from the intergalactic medium. Light or energy are then captured and registered on high quality emulsion films that French cosmonaut Jean-Louis Chrétien collected and returned to Earth for data analysis.

Author Keywords: hotographic equipment, history of manned space flight. Soviet-French cooperation in space

articleTitle: Accounting and Control Are the Basis of Socialism: Computing Technology in USSR (1917-1941)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The report describes the measures taken in the USSR for the production of computing equipment between World Wars, and analyzes their effectiveness. It is shown that the main incentive for the development of their production were the needs of accounting. It is shown also that neither the nomenclature, nor the quantity or quality of mechanical computing devices met the requirements of time, which, probably, together with the appearance of new, extremely complex tasks after the end of the war, stipulated the development of a fundamentally new, electronic computing technology.

articleTitle: Methods and Technologies of Machine Phraseological Translation Based on the Generalized Syntagm Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The studies performed by the authors show that when using the model of generalized syntagmas, it is possible to implement the PMT process using a shorter and simpler technological scheme. This technological scheme can be reduced to two stages: 1) the stage of formation of several search syntagmas characterizing the semantic content of the source text sentences (on the base of results of morphological and simplified syntactic analysis); 2) the stage of searching for semantic information in the reference dictionaries of translations of global and local constructions of sentences, having which it will be possible to automatically form translated sentences of text on their basis. A comparison of the effectiveness of phraseological machine translation using the method of generalized syntagmas and without using it was made.

Author Keywords: syntactic model of language, computer grammar, morphological analysis, semantic and syntactic analysis, formal model of syntactic text structure, generalized syntagmas

articleTitle: Digital Technologies in Architectural Design, Verification and Representation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Digital technologies in the process of architectural design, verification and representation provide innovative tools for the creation of a time-spatial model of the construction as well as the simulation, analytical and evaluation methods of proposed structures from the viewpoint of assessing natural, technical, ecological and socio-economic impacts. In the case of parametric procedural modeling, the specified parameters directly generate spatial structure. Current comprehensive Building Information Modeling systems integrate the creation tools, tools for static and load testing, energy performance and facility management. They provide the ability to parameterize the design and validate it not only in the animation but in virtual reality as well. The methods of augmented reality mediate almost the real perception of the object proposed in the process before its physical construction. The research encompasses the actual trends within this dynamic field, including ethical and legal contexts and the overview of the historical background of its application in the educational process at the Faculty of Architecture Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava.

articleTitle: History of Logarithmic Devices in Russia in the Items of the Polytechnic Museum Collection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The collection "Logarithmic tables and calculating analog devices" is used to study the history of computing technology. This collection is a part of the computer equipment stock of the Polytechnic Museum. This collection contains logarithmic tables and analog logarithmic calculating devices from the first - imperfect, with small computing capabilities, to the more recent - ultra-accurate logarithmic tables, numerous specialized nomograms and slide rulers with advanced scales. The collection demonstrates the main trends of their development, the variety of applications of these devices, their importance in computational practice in various periods of time from the beginning of the 17th century to the end of the 20th. In the collection of "Logarithmic tables and calculating analog devices" of the Polytechnic Museum there are both conventional and precision devices. There are straight logarithmic rules, round rules, round spiral rules, cylinders with a spiral scale, split cylinders, split rules.

Author Keywords: museum, collection, mathematical analogue, devices, Russian logarithmic slide rules

articleTitle: Works on Electric Helicopter in the USSR (1935-1941)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article summarizes the unusual idea of building a tethered helicopter with electric motor for observational purposes. The motors powering the rotors were to be connected to a source of electricity on ground via cable. The author of this scheme was an engineer of the All-Union Electrotechnical Institute, A.G. Iosifjan. Experiments with the apparatus started in the mid-1930s. The work was carried out in three stages. At first, Iosifjan constructed a model with an electric motor powering a coaxially rotors. As a next step, he built a manned vehicle with electric motors placed at the ends of the rotor blades. Finally, in 1940-41, conventional petrol engines installed on a helicopter that had flown before were replaced by electric motors. In terms of the weight-power ratio, these new motors were 10 times lighter compared to traditional ones. The electric helicopter was subjected to real-life tests - it was able to take-off and perform simple flight maneuvers. Due to the war, though, further work was cancelled; development was not resumed after the war.

articleTitle: Topology of Gluing of Virtual and Real Law in Cases of On-Line Crimes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The article describes offenses within Massively Multiplayer Online Worlds (MMOW). The use of criminal law in cases of crimes committed by the inhabitants of virtual worlds is also discussed. But what is considered a crime if it is committed in a virtual world, and under what conditions can there be a real criminal liability? The author offer his answers to these questions. The aim of the article is to draw attention to gaps in law regulating of MMOW's participants conduct. The author also comes to the conclusions that virtual worlds need internal rules and regulations and suggest appropriate algorithm for gluing of virtual and real law in cases of on-line crimes.

Author Keywords: Massive multi-user role-playing online games, Second Life, avatar, end-user license agreement, program code, virtual worlds, criminal law, virtual crimes, elements of a crime,

articleTitle: Informative Symbolic Representations as a Way to Qualitatively Analyze Time Series
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: A qualitative analysis refers to the identification of the qualitative characteristics of a time series, such as its periodicity, final periodicity or near periodicity, convergence to the limit state, randomness, etc. For such an analysis, methods of symbolic dynamics are used, with the time series being represented as a sequence of symbols from a finite alphabet. Such a representation of the time series corresponds to the division of the state space of the process into a finite number of parts, each of which is denoted by a separate symbol. Thus, the symbolic representation of the time series shows in which part of the state space the process is at each moment. The choice of the cardinality of the alphabet of the symbols used affects the dependence between the laboriousness of obtaining the results of the analysis of the time series and their accuracy. To choose the cardinality of the alphabet, it was proposed to use the method of analysis of the entropy of words obtained using a sliding window of variable length. Two approaches that differ in the criterion of splitting are considered: coding of the time series levels based on dividing the range of its values, and coding trends, that is, changes in these values. A method for calculating the entropy function is described. Decision rules are proposed for obtaining various qualitative characteristics of symbolic representations of time series based on the values of the entropy function.

Author Keywords: time series, symbolic analysis, coding, entropy, trends

articleTitle: The Siemens Company Innovative Activity in Electrical Engineering in Russia (1880-1886)
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Within the article the innovative activity of engineering companies on the Russian electric lighting market at the end of the 20th century was analyzed. The phase of industrial revolution that influenced the development of electrical engineering was described in terms of discoveries made in this field. A number of measures to systematize and legitimize the use of the technology were taken. That indicated the completion of the last stage of research in the field of electrical engineering. In line with this trend, electric lighting market in Russia has emerged and that has provided numerous opportunities for technologic advance. In addition, the concept of the innovation as a new combination of productive forces is described. Thus, a new combination is the main source of profit. The study also outlines the Siemens company penetration to the Russian electric lighting market, its marketing policy of the company and its technologies brought to the market over the period.

Author Keywords: electrification of Russia, electric lighting market, the Siemens company in Russia, electrical engineering, electrical engineering innovations, technological innovations

articleTitle: The First Soviet Scientific Papers on Management Information Systems in the RVCM
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The main purpose of the article is to describe a large-scale and so far little-studied layer of the history of Soviet science - the history of the all-Union industry of management information systems (MIS). In the 1960s and 70s in the Soviet Union about seven hundred thousand specialists of various profiles worked for creating and using management information systems (economists, analysts, project managers, algorithmists, programmers, data entry services workers, electronic engineers, computer operators, etc.). It is safe to say that in the USSR, during the specified period of time, a whole independent branch was created and functioned - the MIS industry.

Author Keywords: Management information systems, MIS industry, RVCM, Victor Glushkov, Anatoly Kitov, information retrieval systems, digital technologies,

articleTitle: Researches and Tests of the Aviation Radio-Electronic Equipment in the USSR
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: As you know, electronic equipment on board off the aircraft plays a significant role, especially in cases where the transport operation is not performed, but a special task is solved, for which the aircraft is actually created. Such tasks include the search and detection of the target (air, ground, surface, underwater, disguised, hidden or covered by interference), the use of weapons (controlled or unmanaged), intelligence, radio communication, information collection and exchange it with the ground and other aircraft, search for equipment and people in distress, etc. The capabilities of electronic systems, depending on their purpose and design are great, it is the detection of air, ground, underground, surface and underwater targets, through the clouds and in the fog, at night, object recognition, ensuring the collection and transmission of information on a global scale. These systems are widely used in Geology, cartography, meteorology, rescue operations, inspection of natural resources, etc. Modern electronic systems are complex and expensive devices, the cost of which in some cases exceeds the cost of the aircraft, and the volume and duration of their tests are comparable, and often exceed the volume and duration of the tests of the aircraft itself. Therefore, simultaneously with the development of aviation radio electronics, there is a need for special scientific units specializing in the development and creation of methodological, metrological and instrument support for testing onboard radio electronic systems. The report for the first time describes in detail about the research and testing of various aviation radio-electronic equipment in the units of the Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute, and later-in the Flight research Institute.

articleTitle: Evolution of Data Management Systems and Their Security
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: The paper discusses the evolution of data management systems (up to Big data systems inclusive), the development of security tools, as well as the evolution of vulnerabilities and security features of advanced DBMS.

articleTitle: Social Informatics Challenges Connected with Generational Changes and the Design, Acceptance and Use of ICT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Engineering Technologies and Computer Science (EnT)
abstract: Following various information and communications technology (ICT) or information system design efforts, the issue of ICT acceptance and use by a selected social category is an important theme for a number of academic fields dealing with sociotechnical interaction. One of these areas is social informatics (SI), which connects the social sciences and informatics. SI emerged as a label in various regions, being associated with different historical backgrounds and thematic focus. This paper discusses the impact of generational changes on transformations in sociotechnical interaction from a SI research perspective. With the coming of new generations, there is a need for continuous validation of theories and past conclusions about ICT design, acceptance, and use resulting from previous empirical research. On the other hand, with the aging of current generations and their adaptation to modern ICT, there is a need to create a knowledge base about design approaches appropriate for the capabilities of these generations that arise from the use of ICT. The same can be applied to any other social category, e.g. disadvantaged people. In this respect, the paper draws attention to the need of the US and Western European SI schools of thought to create and validate the theoretical basis of SI across the idea landscape of these schools - an effort which may result in their tighter integration.
